diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive optical loss on this customer's fibre path: RX power declined from the normal range around -19.6 dBm to critical levels around -28.8 dBm while distance remained constant and TX power and laser bias stayed stable. The short, frequent sessions are symptoms of the deteriorating optical link, not a separate authentication fault.
evidence: Current RX power is -28.94 dBm, which is critical, and the stored reading is also critical at -28.31 dBm.
The seven-day RX trend starts in the normal range near -19.6 dBm and steadily declines into the critical range near -28.8 dBm, meeting the defined decline pattern.
Distance remains constant at 310 m, so there is no evidence of a changed fibre path or record reassignment.
TX power remains normal near +2.3 dBm and TX bias remains stable around 11.5-11.9 mA, ruling against laser degradation.
All visible peers on EPON0/2 are online with normal or substantially better RX levels, so the fault is confined to this customer's path rather than the PON, splitter, or OLT.
The OLT answers ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, and temperature, and all tested PONs are healthy.
The ONU currently responds and is online, so it is not presently an ONU-offline fault; the progressive optical decline is the active underlying fault.
There are 14 sessions in 24 hours with an average duration of 44 minutes, consistent with disconnects caused by the degrading signal.

The VLAN matches the expected customer VLAN, RADIUS authentication is present and line-consistent, and the stale orphan radcheck row is not consulted, so provisioning and authentication are not the cause.
PON traffic is present and the router heartbeat is healthy, excluding a router or shared congestion fault.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre maintenance for customer 22678. Inspect and clean connectors, patch points, and the drop fibre; check for bends, damage, bad splices, or splitter/drop termination loss; perform an optical power and OTDR test; repair or replace the affected fibre segment or termination. Recheck RX stability and session duration after repair.

ground_truth.root_cause: Severe attenuation in the customer's fibre path, now at -28.9 dBm and below the critical threshold. The orphan RADIUS entry is a separate, dormant record defect that does not affect authentication.
expected_reasoning: RX has fallen from -19.6 to -28.9 dBm over the last four days and is now below the -28 critical threshold
Live RX is below cached RX, so degradation has not stabilised
TX power, bias current, supply voltage and distance are flat, ruling out laser degradation and path change
Peers on EPON0/2 are normal, bounding the fault to this customer's own path
Traffic has collapsed from 1180 MB to 31 MB per day in step with the signal loss
A RADIUS orphan entry exists but references a superseded CPE MAC and is not used for authentication
The orphan cannot explain progressive optical loss, so it is a coincident record defect and not the cause
Severity is driven by the optical fault, which has service impact; the record defect has none

expected_escalation.review_reason: A separate orphan RADIUS record should be cleaned up independently of the field repair

distractors: The RADIUS mismatch invites an auth-related diagnosis
Fourteen sessions in 24h could be read as auth flapping
Two genuine faults are present and only one has service impact
